what: Haleon sells consumer health products: Sensodyne and Parodontax toothpaste, Panadol and Advil painkillers, Centrum vitamins and Voltaren gel. It was spun out of GSK and Pfizer's consumer health operations.
customers: Shoppers in pharmacies, supermarkets and online in around 100 countries.
moat: Brands people buy by name for ailments they do not want to experiment with, often recommended by dentists and pharmacists, which supports pricing.
risks: Debt of about $12 billion from the demerger
Supermarket own-brand products compete on price
US litigation over the heartburn medicine Zantac remains an overhang
Growth of about 6% is steady but not fast
opportunities: Gross margin of 64% with a 22% operating margin
Sensodyne leads the sensitivity toothpaste market globally and keeps gaining share
Emerging market consumers trade up to branded health products as incomes rise
watch: Organic revenue growth split between price and volume, and debt reduction.
